subject: MAP and evaluation plan: success assertions, exit gates, integration smoke tests
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <apark@helioshealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP and evaluation plan: success assertions, exit gates, integration smoke tests

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. To make the evaluation run smoothly I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) that focuses on measurable acceptance tests and clear exit gates. High-level proposal below — please confirm owners and any hard constraints you need.

Proposed evaluation scope (3 weeks by default):
- Week 1 (Integration smoke): end-to-end request/response using your sample payloads; basic auth + telemetry integration.
- Week 2 (Performance & accuracy): p50/p95 latency sampling, throughput ramp, concordance checks versus your golden set.
- Week 3 (Stability & signoff): soak run, incident playbook verification, final decision meeting.

Suggested success assertions / acceptance tests (draft):
- Latency: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms on demo traffic shape.
- Throughput: sustain 5 rps with target tails (no more than 2% request errors).
- Accuracy/concordance: >= 92% agreement with your annotated set on key intents.
- Cost envelope: projected per-request token cost <= $0.003 (we'll provide breakdown).
- Safety/behavior: hallucination rate (false positive factual claims) < 3% on the eval corpus.

Exit gates (examples):
- Integration smoke completed and checklist verified by Helios dev lead.
- Performance run meets p50/p95 and error-rate thresholds above.
- Security artifacts (SOC 2 summary, KMS integration notes) shared and acceptable.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (mutual action plan), integration-smoke-tests.md (test runner instructions).

Are you able to share the golden evaluation set and a contact for your dev lead to schedule the integration window? If PHI is involved, we can sign a narrow NDA addendum prior to receiving samples.

If 3 weeks is too aggressive we can extend by one week; call out any immovable milestones and we’ll adapt.

Thanks —

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) Data & compliance: we need to understand where sample data will live during the eval. Can Redwood run the evaluation inside our VPC? We may need to keep PHI within our environment.
2) Security artifacts: please share SOC 2 summary + any FedRAMP or healthcare compliance notes you have.
3) Acceptance criteria: we want to add a hallucination/concordance threshold to the acceptance tests — are you able to run the concordance metric against our annotated set (goal >= 92%)?
4) Timeline: 3 weeks is reasonable but engineering would prefer a 4-week window to allow for internal approvals and a formal soak. Is adding a little buffer feasible?

Also copying Tom (integration lead) to confirm he can provide the golden set and schedule the integration run.

Alicia — thanks for the quick reply and the requests. Short answers below and updated notes in the attachment.

1) VPC/private deployment: yes — Redwood Private supports an evaluation inside a customer VPC or dedicated infra for regulated data. If you need on-prem we can discuss a short-term staging appliance, but for most PHI-sensitivity scenarios the VPC path and HSM/KMS options are enough.

2) Security artifacts: attached SOC 2 summary (link in MAP), list of certs, and our security checklist. If you need an NDA addendum for the sample payloads we can route that today.

3) Concordance metric: we can run the concordance analysis against your annotated set. Our suggested pass threshold (>= 92%) is doable for the class of prompts you showed, but we'll run a pre-eval probe to surface edge cases. We'll include per-intent breakdowns so you can see where the model needs prompt or prompt-template adjustments.

4) Timeline buffer: we can move to 4 weeks with an explicit buffer week for approvals/soak. Proposed milestone dates below (draft):
- Integration smoke: target completion 2026-10-24
- Perf + concordance run: target completion 2026-10-31
- Soak & final decision meeting: target completion 2026-11-07 (decision meeting week of 11/8)

Metrics we'll deliver after the perf run: latency distribution (p50/p90/p95), error-rate, concordance heatmap, token cost breakdown, and a short list of mitigations for any failing vignettes.

Link: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/HL-4721 — I'll keep the MAP updated there.

--
Soojin Lee

Hi Alicia — looping in as your CSM for this evaluation. Nice to meet you. I captured owners and operational exit gates below so everyone has clarity: 

Owners:
- Helios integration lead: Tom Nguyen (provide golden set + schedule integration window)
- Redwood SRE owner: Ben Carter (will own perf runs and incident communication)
- Redwood Eval owner: Soojin Lee (test definitions and concordance runs)
- Redwood CSM: Marissa Cole (operational acceptance and logistics)

Mutual action plan milestones (confirmed):
- 2026-10-24: Integration smoke run complete (Tom confirms checklist)
- 2026-10-31: Performance & concordance run complete (Ben and Soojin to present results)
- 2026-11-07: 72-hr soak complete and decision meeting scheduled week of 2026-11-08

Exit gate definitions (operational):
- Integration smoke: all auth & telemetry routes instrumented, no critical integration blockers.
- Performance: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms, <1% error rate, sustain 5 rps for 15 minutes without degradation.
- Concordance: >= 92% overall; any intent < 80% must have a remediation plan with owner and due date.

Rollback criteria (if we fail):
- If critical integration blocking issue persists after 3 business days, trigger rollback to baseline endpoint and schedule a hotfix sprint.

I'll populate the MAP spreadsheet with these owners and dates and share the final doc. If Helios legal needs the NDA addendum, please indicate point of contact and we'll route DocuSign today.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Marissa / Soojin — thanks, that timeline and the ownership breakdown look good to us. A couple final asks before we kick off the smoke run: 

1) Can Redwood provide an automated integration smoke test runner (script or container) so Tom's team can run the suite in our staging environment?
2) We'll need a small sample of the annotated golden set to validate the concordance pipeline. Because it contains PHI we need an NDA addendum in place before sending it. Please route the DocuSign and cc legal@helioshealth.com.

Once we have the runner and the NDA addendum we'll schedule the smoke window for next Friday (2026-10-22) or the following Monday (2026-10-25) depending on Redwood's availability.
